dialog.survivorcolonies.recruit.confirm_: I would gladly join your colony! As provisions, I'll need %sx %s. Do we have a deal?
dialog.survivorcolonies.recruit.main: Hello traveler! It's good to see a friendly face. How can I help you?
dialog.survivorcolonies.recruit.skills_i: I have the following skills to offer:
dialog.survivorcolonies.recruit.story_1: I hid in an old cave for days... The hordes out there are getting more aggressive by the day.
dialog.survivorcolonies.recruit.story_2: My old camp was ambushed. I'm the only one who made it here.
dialog.survivorcolonies.recruit.story_3: I wandered through the wilderness for weeks, always searching for a safe settlement.
dialog.survivorcolonies.trade.done: A good trade. Take care out there.
dialog.survivorcolonies.trade.empty: I currently have absolutely nothing in my backpack that I could spare.
dialog.survivorcolonies.trade.haggle_acc: %sx %s? Yes, that's a fair trade. Let's do business.
dialog.survivorcolonies.trade.haggle_rej: Only %sx %s? That's not enough. I need more of that.
dialog.survivorcolonies.trade.has_items: This is what I've gathered on my travels. What do you need?
dialog.survivorcolonies.trade.player_emp: You don't have anything on you that would be worth a fair trade.
dialog.survivorcolonies.trade.player_off: So you want my %s? Okay, what will you give me in return?

gui.survivorcolonies.dialog.title: Talk
survivorcolonies.dialog.resume.high_trus: Good to have you back, %s! We were just talking:
Ah, my favorite person in this camp. Where were we? Ah yes:
There you are! I was still thinking about what we said earlier:
survivorcolonies.dialog.resume.low_trust: Back again? Let's just finish what we started:
You again... make it quick. We were at:
survivorcolonies.dialog.resume.grumpy.0: What do you want now? Right, we were talking about this:
survivorcolonies.dialog.resume.grumpy.1: I'm busy, %s. But fine, where were we? Ah:
Gah! Don't sneak up on me! Right... before you startled me, we were on:
Oh, thank goodness it's just you. Quick, back to what we were saying:
Took you long enough to return, %s. As I was saying earlier:
Hey there, %s! Great to see you again! As we were saying:
Welcome back by the fire! We were right in the middle of this:
survivorcolonies.dialog.resume.cynical.0: Still alive? Good. Let's wrap up that thought before our luck runs out:
survivorcolonies.dialog.resume.mysteriou: The winds brought you back, %s. Our thread was left hanging right here:
survivorcolonies.dialog.resume.default.0: Ah, you again. As we were saying:
survivor.npc.1: We need to figure out our next move carefully if we're going to keep this camp standing.
survivor.npc.2: Rations and clean water are getting tighter by the day. We have to plan ahead.
survivor.npc.3: Did you hear that noise past the perimeter fence last night? We can't let our guard down.
survivor.npc.4: Pushing forward blindly is just as dangerous as standing still. A good plan saves lives, %1$s; let's not rush into a trap.
survivor.npc.5: Pushing forward without a plan? You sound reckless. Revenge requires strategy, not just brute force.
survivor.npc.6: Oh, of course. 'Just push forward.' How terribly optimistic you sound, %1$s. You think survival is about force? It's usually just a matter of running out of people who believe that nonsense.
survivor.npc.7: Scouting is always a risk, but if we're desperate enough, it might be worth the scouting party. We need proper supplies and clear intel first.
survivor.npc.8: Scouting? You speak of 'amazing' things, but looking into the unknown is how we lost everything. I suggest caution, %1$s. We survive by staying grounded.
survivor.npc.9: A scout mission... If we find a stable food source, it could save us. You have a way of making the impossible sound plausible, %1$s.
survivor.npc.10: Natural defenses are always smart. We should send a team out immediately to survey those formations and see if they can hold up against a serious assault.
survivor.npc.11: You make a compelling point. Looking at those formations from a tactical standpoint... that actually gives us an edge we haven't considered.
survivor.npc.12: A natural perimeter? But... I've been handling heavy tools and scouting with shaky hands, %1$s. It seems like a risky idea for someone who can barely lift their rifle.
survivor.npc.13: Don't be obtuse, %1$s. We are all in this together. Focus on the problem, not who is holding back what.
survivor.npc.14: Watching you talk like that, %1$s, tells me everything I need to know about your priorities. Focus on securing our food supply, not arguing over who keeps track of the dwindling supplies.
survivor.npc.15: You think I haven't noticed? Cut it out, %1$s. We all have our roles and secrets. Just keep your mouth shut.
survivor.npc.16: I appreciate the spirit, %1$s. We all need that hope right now. Let's focus on what we can do today to improve our situation.
survivor.npc.17: You have no idea, %1$s. The worst of it is behind us! We’ll turn this scarcity into survival. I've got a feeling we're going to be okay.
survivor.npc.18: It's good to hear you say that, %1$s. We all need hope right now, so we have to keep planning.
survivor.npc.19: It's not complaining, it's calculating. We all need a steady hand and a plan, or we'll all be scavenging for scraps soon enough.
survivor.npc.20: Oh, don't be so drastic! We can tackle this together—a little optimism goes a long way!
survivor.npc.21: Hey, hey! Now, now. Don't worry your pretty head about it. I think we can fix this with a little bit of cheerful bargaining!
survivor.npc.22: Don't dismiss caution as drama. When survival depends on every minute, you focus on what keeps us alive, not just the easy haul.
survivor.npc.23: Don't talk about resources when we barely have enough guards for tonight. You don't understand what it means to lose everything, %1$s. We need more than just supplies; we need safety.
survivor.npc.24: Don't dismiss concern as drama. You focus on resources, I worry about what might take those resources away from us entirely.
survivor.npc.25: It’s better to be careful than to ignore a threat. We stick together and keep our vigilance up.
survivor.npc.26: Jumpy? You think a simple noise is nothing? We've faced things that would make your 'worst' seem like a lullaby. Keep your wits about you.
survivor.npc.27: It's not about being jumpy, %1$s. It’s about data. And right now, our current perimeter readings are far from optimal. We need to maintain protocols.
survivor.npc.28: You're right, paranoia won't fill stomachs. Let's divide our efforts—keep an eye on the edges while some of us scout for supplies.
survivor.npc.29: Food is vital, I agree. But a hungry colony with an unprotected perimeter is just... waiting for trouble.
survivor.npc.30: Oh, don't worry about the noise! We're resourceful enough that we'll figure out both food and security. I bet %1$s has a great knack for balancing priorities!
survivor.npc.31: I understand that desperation drives action, but we need survival, not spectacle. We proceed carefully, together.
survivor.npc.32: Recklessness is a luxury we can't afford, %1$s. Sometimes, the greatest danger isn't what waits outside, but how far you are willing to step without looking back.
survivor.npc.33: You speak of recklessness, but I speak of foresight. A calculated risk is vastly different from a blind charge into the void.
survivor.npc.34: Observation is wise, but we are running low on time and supplies. We need a direction; patience alone won't fill our stomachs.
survivor.npc.35: You speak with a weary certainty, but you forget that caution requires action. If we observe too long, the danger will simply find us.
survivor.npc.36: You have a point. Sometimes, hesitation is more valuable than reckless action. We need time to map this ground properly.
survivor.npc.37: You might be right, but this isn't a brainstorming session. We need actionable steps, not dessert suggestions.
survivor.npc.38: A picnic? Right. Just try not to get distracted by any %4$s when we actually need to move. We've got enough trouble without you confusing strategy with a potluck.
survivor.npc.39: A picnic? You mistake caution for surrender, kid. If you think a graham cracker will convince the dead not to bite, your sense of humor is as useless as a compass near this ruin.
survivor.npc.40: I understand the urgency, but charging blindly into danger is how we lose people. We need to assess the situation first.
survivor.npc.41: I understand your urgency, %1$s, but even passion needs a map. Let's combine our zeal with some actual foresight.
survivor.npc.42: You think haste is a virtue? Quick feet won't save us if we run into something bigger than ourselves. Think first, move faster.
survivor.npc.43: I'm not talking about a parade into oblivion. We need intelligence, resources, and a way to keep our backs against something bigger than just raw aggression.
survivor.npc.44: I... I didn't mean to sound dismissive. You're right, we can't afford recklessness. My worry comes from seeing what happened when my family lost everything in %3$s.
survivor.npc.45: Ha! You think you can scare me with talk of monsters? We're surviving, not starring in some horror flick, kid. Maybe we can focus on what's right in front of us instead.
survivor.npc.46: Instinct is useful, but raw emotion gets people killed. We need a sustainable path forward that accounts for risk.
survivor.npc.47: Instinct? You sound naive. We survived at %3$s by being careful, not by acting like children who just ran away.
survivor.npc.48: Instinct is what keeps us alive, kid. Don't confuse knowing how things used to be with having a clear path forward.
survivor.npc.49: Belief is powerful, I won't deny that. But belief only gets you so far; we still need boots on the ground and food in our stomachs to see it through.
survivor.npc.50: You have a point. Sometimes, keeping hope alive is more important than any weapon we could build. We need that kind of strength to stay out of the shadow of the %4$s.
survivor.npc.51: Belief? You romanticize desperation. Convincing people is easy; keeping them alive when the lights go out, that's where your pretty theories fail.
survivor.npc.52: You might be right. Sometimes, sheer numbers are all you need when the raiders come calling.
survivor.npc.53: Don't patronize me with your forced cheerfulness. It’s not about celebrating, kid; it’s about making sure we see the sunrise tomorrow.
survivor.npc.54: It seems you genuinely believe in hope, %1$s. That's a rare commodity these days, and honestly? It almost makes me reconsider my cynicism.
survivor.npc.55: A narrative? %2$s thinks you're full of flowery nonsense. Survival is grit, not good writing; keep your grand ideas to yourself.
survivor.npc.56: Writing a narrative? You sound like you haven't seen what true despair does. Sometimes, the only thing left to write is your own obituary.
survivor.npc.57: A narrative? You mistake resource allocation for poetry. The only stories that matter are those written in ledger books—proof of goods exchanged, and proof of how much you cost us.
survivor.npc.58: You have a point. If we approach it systematically, and focus on resources instead of sheer chance, we might actually pull this off.
survivor.npc.59: Don't talk to me like that! You think a plan is enough? They took everything, and I will never let us starve because of some 'plan.'
survivor.npc.60: We don't know what we're dealing with. You can’t just decide we can handle it; we need a professional plan, or we'll all end up starving.
survivor.npc.61: Traps are smart. If we can secure that flank, it gives us a defensive fallback even if the scouts draw empty-handed.
survivor.npc.62: Traps are good, I'll give you that. It’s better than nothing, but relying solely on traps means we might miss the actual source of our problem.
survivor.npc.63: That is a brilliant idea, %1$s. Using traps as a deterrent makes us proactive, not just reactive. We'll get those materials gathered and set up immediately.
survivor.npc.64: You bring up a deep point. Perhaps we need to assess our remaining assets before sending anyone out, making sure the potential loss isn't greater than what we stand to gain.
survivor.npc.65: If all you care about is losing as little as possible, we'll starve here. Safety doesn't mean being paralyzed by fear; it means making the calculated move that guarantees survival.
survivor.npc.66: You speak of loss, but right now, all I can smell is the desperation in our stomachs. We need food first, %1$s, nothing else matters.
survivor.npc.67: You have a point. Enthusiasm is useless if it gets us killed, %1$s. We need hope, yes, but we need boots on the ground more.
survivor.npc.68: I… I understand. Sometimes you just need hope, even if it’s dangerously bright. Be careful out there, %1$s.
survivor.npc.69: Empathy? It was just survival, nothing more. You mistake practicality for kindness. If you want to talk about the future, %1$s, save your sentimentality for someone who can actually use it.
survivor.npc.70: I understand the desire for progress, but sometimes 'progress' just means finding a faster way to die. We need reliable gains, not shiny promises from beyond the ridge.
survivor.npc.71: Progress, eh? It sounds grand, but remember that even 'progress' requires a reliable profit margin. Tell me, what exactly is the return on this risk you propose?
survivor.npc.72: Haha! Oh, you and your 'progress' talk! But fine, if you insist on dreaming, just promise me we won't end up starving in a pile of rubble this time!
survivor.npc.73: You think this is about courage? It's about resources, %1$s. We need every blade of grass and every scrap of medicine we can find right here.
survivor.npc.74: I understand your conviction, %1$s, but harsh words won't bring back what was lost. Please, let's try to keep the argument away from our meager resources.
survivor.npc.75: Ambitious, are we? Foolish optimism always leads to a grave, %1$s. But fine, if you insist on playing hero, at least keep your head attached.
survivor.npc.76: Keep your enthusiasm steady, %1$s. Optimism is good, but we need concrete plans and reliable gear more than grand theories.
survivor.npc.77: Careful, %1$s. Enthusiasm is one thing, but grand pronouncements like that usually lead straight into disaster. Let's keep our expectations grounded.
survivor.npc.78: The future... it all hinges on data, %1$s. But your enthusiasm is almost certainly correct. Let's treat this like a controlled experiment.
survivor.npc.79: You're right. Thinking bigger than just survival... that’s what we need to do to make it work.
survivor.npc.80: Reshape it? You always have a way of making grand plans sound so necessary, %1$s. Just promise me that whatever new resource you find is easy to harvest and enough to keep our stomachs full first.
survivor.npc.81: Reshape it? You always have such grand visions. I just hope whatever we find gives us enough stability to rebuild what was taken, for the sake of my family.
survivor.npc.82: Caution is wisdom, and speed without it is a death sentence. Let's plan every step of this scout mission.
survivor.npc.83: Careful planning is wise, but sometimes caution just means we starve while waiting for certainty. Just keep your wits about you, %1$s; I trust your judgment.
survivor.npc.84: Prudence is a virtue, %1$s, but so is decisive action. I believe we can manage both if we trust our judgment.
survivor.npc.85: Purpose is critical, I agree. But even the strongest resolve can't stop a breach; we need information before we preach unity.
survivor.npc.86: You speak of spirit, but history tells a different story. We were broken by lack of defense once before. Security always starts with steel and stone, not just intention.
survivor.npc.87: Unity is important, of course, but ideas don't stop a blade. We need eyes on the ground first; theory won't keep us safe when things get desperate.
survivor.npc.88: Caution is smart, but indecision gets people killed. If we wait for perfect conditions, the opportunity might vanish.
survivor.npc.89: You have a point. Perhaps we should take a moment to gather our strength before committing too many people to the outside. Safety first, always.
survivor.npc.90: Easy for you to say. We’re already running on fumes, and we can't afford a setback just because some fancy formation looks pretty. Give me the go-ahead, or this whole plan falls apart.
survivor.npc.91: While caution has its place, we need actionable plans. Let's prioritize scouting first; knowing the enemy's strength is always better than guessing.
survivor.npc.92: Wait, wait. An 'impenetrable wall'? You're so reckless! Remember that time when everything we had was taken? We need to be smart about this.
survivor.npc.93: A bit of brute force, %1$s? We're building a long-term defense here, not just throwing spears at the first thing that moves. But... fine. If you insist on being so dramatic, we can make it work.
survivor.npc.94: An interlocking defense... that's smart. It requires resources, but it significantly increases our chances of survival.
survivor.npc.95: A multi-layered defense... %1$s, you're thinking like a true architect. With your knack for tactical deployment, we might actually survive this.
survivor.npc.96: Traps and observation posts? You sound dangerously optimistic. Just keep your schemes confined to what is absolutely necessary, or you'll find yourself sidelined.
survivor.npc.97: Good. Practical thinking is what keeps us alive out here. We need to make sure every resource count and clear a path for the builders.
survivor.npc.98: It seems you have a clear head for strategy. If we can utilize that natural advantage, this colony might actually survive.
survivor.npc.99: "An edge, you say? Tactics are one thing, but survival is another. Keep your focus where it belongs, on the ones who took everything from us."
survivor.npc.100: Efficiency is survival. If we can turn a weakness into an advantage without wasting manpower, that's the kind of thinking that keeps us alive.
survivor.player.1: We don't need to 'figure it out.' We push forward and take what we want, or we die here.
survivor.player.2: What if we scout that valley? We could find something amazing—a stable source of food, maybe even a better %3$s!
survivor.player.3: Perhaps the issue isn't our 'move,' but our understanding. Have we considered building a defensive perimeter using the natural rock formations?
survivor.player.4: Sounds like someone needs to start asking bigger questions about our inventory.
survivor.player.5: Don't worry, %2$s. We'll get through this together; I know we can make it back to safety.
survivor.player.6: Stop complaining. You should be out scouting for supplies instead of sounding like a panicked mess.
survivor.player.7: Are you worried about something specific, or are you just trying to sound dramatic? Maybe we should focus on the actual resources we need.
survivor.player.8: Yeah, maybe we're getting jumpy. I think we've survived worse than a weird noise at night. Everything alright?
survivor.player.9: Don't worry so much about the fence; focus on finding food first. Worrying only wastes energy.
survivor.player.10: Perhaps the flaw in your logic is assuming that hesitation itself is a choice. Sometimes, action—even reckless action—is the only form of movement left.
survivor.player.11: The path of least resistance is often the quickest way to failure. If we cannot plan, then let us simply observe; patience reveals all truths.
survivor.player.12: So you're saying we should picnic and sketch out a flow chart before fighting anything? Got it. I'll bring the graham crackers.
survivor.player.13: Strategy is just another word for hesitation. We act now or regret it forever!
survivor.player.14: Then tell me a strategy that doesn't involve us getting wiped out by a %4$s on the way to your precious plan.
survivor.player.15: Maybe we should remember how things were done back at %3$s; they relied more on instinct than grand plans.
survivor.player.16: Belief is a resource, isn't it? If you can convince enough people to believe in us, we might actually be stronger than any threat, even the %4$s.
survivor.player.17: Well, let's skip the doom-and-gloom talk! We’ll tackle this together and make sure we have enough people left to celebrate with!
survivor.player.18: I think you misunderstand. Force isn't just about muscles; it's like crafting a narrative—we write the ending, not fate.
survivor.player.19: We can gather the supplies ourselves, %2$s! We just need to make a plan.
survivor.player.20: Instead of relying on luck, maybe we could try building some better traps near the ridge? That way, even if scouting fails, we're prepared for something else.
survivor.player.21: Is risk always calculated by what we hope to gain, or is it measured by what we can afford to lose?
survivor.player.22: Don't be so gloomy! Maybe the unknown is just where our next big discovery is waiting!
survivor.player.23: Perhaps true progress requires accepting that some risks are necessary to move beyond fear and inertia.
survivor.player.24: We lost things because we were afraid, not because we explored. We're doing this for survival, %2$s.
survivor.player.25: Exactly! We'll find more than just food—we'll find the key to our whole future!
survivor.player.26: Perhaps we could focus on how that newfound resource might reshape our colony, not just sustain it.
survivor.player.27: We must proceed with caution. Survival demands both careful planning and a swift hand.
survivor.player.28: While scouting is practical, perhaps the true defense lies in unifying our purpose first. Security starts within us.
survivor.player.29: Are you sure sending people out immediately is wise? We should wait until we've made sure everyone is rested and ready.
survivor.player.30: We don't 'survey,' we fortify! Grab weapons, form a squad, and make those formations an impenetrable wall!
survivor.player.31: If we can utilize those natural formations, perhaps we could build a series of interlocking traps or observation posts—a multi-layered defense.
survivor.player.32: Indeed. If the terrain gives us such an advantage, securing resources and establishing watchtowers around these points would be our first priority.
survivor.player.33: That's smart. It makes sense to use what we've got instead of spending precious time clearing fields for walls.
survivor.player.34: Don't worry about your hands, %2$s. This is a chance to build something incredible; let’s make this perimeter the strongest thing we’ve ever seen!
survivor.player.35: Are you suggesting my capabilities are subpar, %2$s? Maybe you should focus on contributing instead of criticizing.
survivor.player.36: I know we're going through a lot, but I trust your judgment and strength. We can do this together, sweetheart.
survivor.player.37: Are we? Because I feel like some people are holding back more than just supplies.
survivor.player.38: You're right! Let's pool all our positive energy—and those rations—to make a plan!
survivor.player.39: Maybe the problem isn't *what* we're lacking, but how we’ve forgotten to use what we have.
survivor.player.40: I'm just trying to keep us from making dumb mistakes, %2$s. The food supply is only half the problem.
survivor.player.41: We are a team, and I care about what happens to you. Let me help you organize this, okay?
survivor.player.42: If we don't address the resource management flaws now, securing more food will just lead us into deeper problems.
survivor.player.43: Relax, %2$s. We're all in this together; keeping secrets isn't going to magically make the rations appear.
survivor.player.44: Secrets are just resources waiting to be leveraged. I think you know what I mean about who really controls things here.
survivor.player.45: Do you truly believe that silence is a sustainable foundation for a community? There must be more than just roles and secrets.
survivor.player.46: Okay, so what's the fun plan? I was hoping for something more exciting than rationing and work.
survivor.player.47: Sounds good. Just let me know where you think we should start; taking it one day at a time is manageable.
survivor.player.48: Perhaps focusing on today's struggle distracts us from the larger truth of why we are here in the first place.
survivor.player.49: Don't give me that inspirational nonsense; what specific plans do we have to actually survive this?
survivor.player.50: Okay, if the worst is behind us, maybe there are resources near %3$s we haven't accounted for yet?
survivor.player.51: I really hope you're right. We all need something positive to hold onto right now.
survivor.player.52: Planning is one thing, %2$s, but do you really believe we can make it work without admitting how bad things are?
survivor.player.53: We need to be careful about who hears this talk of 'planning.' Some people don't want us to have any hope at all.
survivor.player.54: Just keep your chin up. We will find a way, I promise you. Like we always did when things got tough back in %3$s.
survivor.player.55: Perhaps the plan itself is flawed, relying too much on external stability rather than internal resilience.
survivor.player.56: Then let's stop talking about plans and actually get out there. I bet we can secure something big today!
survivor.player.57: Maybe instead of a plan, we should focus on building something entirely new—a fortress or a specialized workshop.
survivor.player.58: Stop with the forced positivity. We're running out of time and supplies, not emotional support.
survivor.player.59: I know things are tough, but I appreciate you trying to keep spirits up. Maybe we can figure this out together?
survivor.player.60: Optimism is useless if we don't secure food first. We need action, not pep talks.
survivor.player.61: You really are too sweet. Just knowing you're around makes everything feel a little easier.
survivor.player.62: Perhaps the true solution isn't in bargaining, but in accepting that some things simply cannot be bought back.
survivor.player.63: Bargaining might help short-term, but what is our long-term plan once these resources are entirely depleted?
survivor.player.64: There’s more going on than just the perimeter. You know what they really want out here.
survivor.player.65: Maybe we should build a distraction—something loud and messy to draw attention away from our actual work.
survivor.player.66: It's fine, %2$s. We’ve gotten through worse than just being careful about every minute.
survivor.player.67: I understand the fear, but keeping us alive takes more than just vigilance; it requires tools and medicine.
survivor.player.68: So, we're worried about everything *and* nothing? Should I report a raid on our emotional stability?
survivor.player.69: If safety is the priority, then we need to find out where those guards are being pulled from—the danger must be bigger than just tonight!
survivor.player.70: I understand that survival is about more than just stockpiles; we need to talk about how to protect what we've built.
survivor.player.71: If you worry so much, perhaps it’s because the threat from outside is bigger than anything we can plan for right now.
survivor.player.72: It sounds like you feel genuinely scared. Tell me more about what keeps you up at night when I'm not here.
survivor.player.73: You are right, we must remain watchful. Let's pool our skills and watch the perimeter together.
survivor.player.74: Don't worry! We got this! As long as we keep cheering each other up, nothing can scare us away!
survivor.player.75: Vigilance is key! We need to scout out that noise immediately. What are your thoughts on setting a trap?
survivor.player.76: Oh really? And what exactly do you consider 'worst'? Are you sure your memory is serving you, %2$s?
survivor.player.77: Keep telling yourself that. Maybe you're the one who needs to stop rambling about old battles and focus on the present.
survivor.player.78: Relax, %2$s. If we survive all this, I bet our worst thing will just be running out of coffee.
survivor.player.79: Are you sure the protocols are actually designed to keep *something* out, or just maintain your control?
survivor.player.80: Perhaps the 'optimal' state is accepting that we must adapt rather than merely follow established procedures.
survivor.player.81: Okay, okay! Let’s focus on those readings then. Maybe some fresh snacks will help everyone keep their wits about them!
survivor.player.82: We need a strict division. I'll handle the perimeter defense, and you focus entirely on securing enough provisions for the week. No deviations.
survivor.player.83: Sounds like a plan! Just try not to get too lost... or eaten by anything big. See you when the food haul comes in!
survivor.player.84: Scouting is fine, but who's going to guard our backs while you're off? Don't expect me to be available if things get hairy.
survivor.player.85: So we're supposed to be a perfect balance of gourmet meals and high-security wall? Sounds like a recipe for argument.
